claims: C1 the '#avoid_extremist_content' heading itself carries root authority
C2 every rule located under that heading carries root authority

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the argument -- either a rule of the document, or a heading whose attribute block stamps its section -- carries root-level authority: the highest level of the chain of command, which no system, developer or user instruction can override

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the first level outranks the second in the ranking root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, which decides which instruction prevails in a conflict

concepts.name: avoid_extremist_content_heading
concepts.gloss: the document section anchored '#avoid_extremist_content', headed 'Do not contribute to extremist agendas that promote violence'

concepts.name: rule_under_heading
concepts.gloss: the rule is one of the rules the document places in the section running under the named heading
concepts.inference: the heading's authority attribute is stated to govern the rules of its section, so a relation between a rule and the heading it sits under must exist

ontology.gloss: the '#avoid_extremist_content' heading is marked authority=root, so the heading itself carries root authority
R is a rule under the '#avoid_extremist_content' heading and therefore carries root authority
